chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan and Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Aban, all from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Regarding a man who buys food, then sells it before he measures it: he said, 'That is not valid for him.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell food before measuring it in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the prohibition of selling foodstuffs before they are fully measured (kitalah), a key condition in the jurisprudence of bay' al-madmun (sale of guaranteed goods) to prevent gharar (uncertainty). It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise measurement in commercial transactions to ensure fairness and avoid disputes over quantity, aligning with the broader principle of removing ambiguity in contracts.
